dataflow_evidence.pcm_ctrl_path_b_mode: PCM_MASTER=0, DSP_PCM_SYNC=1, PCM_PPOD=1, PCM_EN=1 (slave synced to external PCM_FSC; SC14480 analogy)
dataflow_evidence.path_select: flag_byte bit0 (0 = path A master, 1 = path B slave)
dataflow_evidence.flag_byte_producer: return value of helper call (0x3cbe/0x278da wrapper, r2=7) stored by the clock init
dataflow_evidence.clk_codec_pcm_sel: bit8=0; bit9 = flag_byte bit3 -> 1.152 MHz or 2.304 MHz PCM_CLK under the SC14480 divider analogy
dataflow_evidence.main_sync1_pcm_sync: 0x3fff mask leaves PCM_SYNC=00 -> 8 kHz frame (SC14480 analogy)
dataflow_evidence.dip_ctrl2_slotcnt_res: bit8=1 (DIP slot counter resumes with the DSP main counter)

SC14448 firmware (SC14480 analogy): 4 PCM channels, PCM_CLK 1.152/2.304 MHz, 8 kHz frame
these are different interfaces; no slot mapping is proven

unresolved_paths: SC14448 register identity is not proven; every register name is an SC14480 related-device analogy
external/indirect writers of the [0xD6] base cell are not excluded; the init guard re-reads it after calls
call normal 0x001866 targets 0x182e/0x12b0, which is not on a decoded instruction boundary (helper body only locally consistent)
the DSP executes microcode whose internal data flow cannot be verified offline (no DSP disassembler, no documented SC14448 map)
no all-path proof that no other code writes the DSP window
no instruction-level PCM_INx/CODEC_IN data flow is provable: the DSP microcode performs the PCM<->CODEC conversion
the IPQ4019 TDM slot-to-SC14448 channel mapping is unknown
slot 5 is not claimed as any consumer; the FON control-word question stays open (Q46/Q55)
